To evaluate the determinant of the matrix 
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
1 & x & y \\ 
1 & x + y & y \\ 
1 & x & x + y 
\end{vmatrix},
\]
we will use cofactor expansion along the first row. The determinant is given by:
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 
1 & x & y \\ 
1 & x + y & y \\ 
1 & x & x + y 
\end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot \begin{vmatrix} x + y & y \\ x & x + y \end{vmatrix} - x \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1 & y \\ 1 & x + y \end{vmatrix} + y \cdot \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x + y \\ 1 & x \end{vmatrix}.
\]

First, we compute each of the 2x2 determinants:
\[
\begin{vmatrix} x + y & y \\ x & x + y \end{vmatrix} = (x + y)(x + y) - y \cdot x = x^2 + 2xy + y^2 - xy = x^2 + xy + y^2,
\]
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 1 & y \\ 1 & x + y \end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot (x + y) - y \cdot 1 = x + y - y = x,
\]
\[
\begin{vmatrix} 1 & x + y \\ 1 & x \end{vmatrix} = 1 \cdot x - (x + y) \cdot 1 = x - x - y = -y.
\]

Substituting these back into the expression for the determinant, we get:
\[
1 \cdot (x^2 + xy + y^2) - x \cdot x + y \cdot (-y) = x^2 + xy + y^2 - x^2 - y^2 = xy.
\]

Thus, the value of the determinant is 
\[
\boxed{xy}.
\]
